Would you be able to clarify if this error is related to insufficient data in the remaining files and if the error affects the integrity of the reduced data in part 5?

Any suggestions on how to overcome this error would be much appreciated.

Thanks,

Dominika

messages.subject: Re: Error: In if (!is.na(sleeponset_prev_loc)) sleeponset_loc[2] = sleeponset_prev_loc[1] :   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
parts:
Hi Dominika,

These warning message relates to some recent updates that we've been making to the plot5 functionality. They are only warnings and your code probably ran fine on all your data.

Basically, they are coming up because we are doing a boolean test on an element that can be a vector sometimes.  I guess R doesn't like this, so we can work on a different way of performing these tests. Even though R throws up the warning, the code still works fine, so all of your results should be good. Note that this warning only relates to generating plots. Check to see that all of your data is processed properly.

I beleive that other users were getting a similar warning with the 'match_loc' variable due to the same issue.

Here is some more information on the warning we are getting - 

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14170778/interpreting-condition-has-length-1-warning-from-if-function

Matt

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Error: In if (!is.na(sleeponset_prev_loc)) sleeponset_loc[2] = sleeponset_prev_loc[1] :   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
parts:
Hi Matt,
This is not good. Warnings are there for a reason and this could lead to unpredictable behavior.

If wake_loc has a length longer than 1 than testing whether it equals 0 means that it tests whether every element in the vector equals zero and returns a new vector of those results.
R does this intentionally because testing every element in a vector is a useful element. To avoid this, always first test whether the length is 1 and then whether the value is 0, or change the test such that it does:
wake_loc == rep(0,length(wake_loc) in case you are interested to know whether all elements of wake_loc are zero.

Can you correct this? 
Thanks, Vincent

‐‐‐‐‐‐‐ Original Message ‐‐‐‐‐‐‐
On Friday, April 17, 2020 2:09 AM, Matt Patterson <patte...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Dominika,

These warning message relates to some recent updates that we've been making to the plot5 functionality. They are only warnings and your code probably ran fine on all your data.

Basically, they are coming up because we are doing a boolean test on an element that can be a vector sometimes.  I guess R doesn't like this, so we can work on a different way of performing these tests. Even though R throws up the warning, the code still works fine, so all of your results should be good. Note that this warning only relates to generating plots. Check to see that all of your data is processed properly.

I beleive that other users were getting a similar warning with the 'match_loc' variable due to the same issue.

Here is some more information on the warning we are getting - 

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14170778/interpreting-condition-has-length-1-warning-from-if-function

Matt
